title: 2021 AMC 10A Problem 16
statement: In the following list of numbers, the integer \(n\) appears \(n\) times in the list for \(1\leq n\leq200.\) \[ \begin{aligned} &1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,4,4,\ldots,\\ &200,200,\ldots,200 \end{aligned} \] What is the median of the numbers in this list?

solutions.text:
The list contains \[ \begin{aligned} 1+2+\cdots+200&=\frac{200\cdot201}{2}\\ &=20100 \end{aligned} \] entries, so its two middle positions are \(10050\) and \(10051.\)

There are \[\frac{141\cdot142}{2}=10011\] entries through the last \(141,\) and \[\frac{142\cdot143}{2}=10153\] entries through the last \(142.\) Thus both middle entries are \(142,\) so the median is \(142.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Locate the two middle positions using triangular numbers
